summary: @ornikar/jest-config-react-native preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package declares a `preinstall` lifecycle hook (`node setup.mjs`) that runs automatically at `npm install`. `setup.mjs` is itself obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style hex-named identifiers such as `_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`, and dispatch-object wrappers around `execFileSync`, `writeFileSync`, and HTTPS download primitives). It downloads a pinned Bun release from github.com/oven-sh/bun to a temp directory, extracts it, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync` to run the sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a ~727KB single-line Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) containing a rotated numeric/string opcode array and a dispatch shuffler (`WV8StW`). This payload is never loaded by the normal Node.js require path; it is only reachable through the freshly downloaded alternate runtime. A jest configuration package has no functional need for a second JavaScript runtime, an obfuscated preinstall script, or a 727KB opaque compiled bundle. Fetching Bun specifically to execute an obfuscated sibling artifact at install time deliberately evades Node-based static analysis and yields arbitrary code execution on the installing machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
